excerpt_i18n.en: There are moments when one can feel time folding: when the footsteps of predecessors meet the hurried pace of successors, and the two draw close and resonate within the same room. On August 7, 2020, during the "Commemorating Thomas S. Huang—40 Years of Legacy in Chinese Computer Vision" session at the Fifth GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit, Harry Shum, Yang Shiqiang, Chen Changwen, Zhang Zhengyou, Tian Qi, Yan Shuicheng, and others recounted the "40-year legacy" as follows: In 2006, Thomas S. Huang attended a Christmas event organized by Quan Long in Hong Kong and coincidentally discovered that several leading figures in computer vision present at the gathering were each exactly ten years apart in age—Thomas S. Huang (born 1936), Ma Songde (born 1946), Gao Wen (born 1956), and Harry Shum (born 1966). Subsequently, they discussed whether they could find another leading figure in computer vision ten years younger at their next gathering. The discussion quickly pointed to the same person: Sun Jian (born 1976), Harry Shum's distinguished protégé. The protagonists of this story—Ma Songde, Gao Wen, Harry Shum, and Sun Jian—have also been regular attendees of GAIR over the years, gathering there due to legacy and mentorship. Each time they see young people in the GAIR audience with tears in their eyes or young scholars writing in the live stream comments, "This is what I aspire to become," they are filled with anticipation, waiting for these young people, both on-site and behind screens, to take up the torch of this legacy. On December 12, 2025, at Bolin Tianrui, Nanshan, Shenzhen.
excerpt_i18n.es: Hay momentos en los que uno puede sentir cómo se pliega el tiempo: cuando los pasos de quienes van delante se encuentran con el apresurado caminar de quienes vienen detrás, y ambos se acercan y resuenan en una misma sala. items.title: DiT-Air: Revisiting the Efficiency of Diffusion Model Architecture Design in Text to Image Generation
items.raw_excerpt: In this work, we empirically study Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for text-to-image generation, focusing on architectural choices, text-conditioning strategies, and training protocols.
